subject.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — core event contracts

question: Should OpenClaw adopt these six AI-safety events as a permanent core and Plugin SDK contract, with plugin emission allowed only through a dedicated policy-gated API?
rationale: The choice fixes public event names, payload semantics, privacy rules, versioning, and a security-sensitive plugin authorization boundary that cannot safely be inferred from implementation quality alone.

options.title: Approve a narrowed contract
options.body: Sponsor the taxonomy after the trusted-emitter bypass is removed, schemaVersion is embedded in every event, and the dedicated plugin authorization API is reviewed with focused compatibility proof.

options.title: Keep events core-internal
options.body: Land no public Plugin SDK event types yet and allow only core-owned producers until the taxonomy has operational experience and stable privacy rules.

options.title: Pause the series
options.body: Do not establish a core taxonomy now; keep safety detectors and exports plugin-owned until a concrete missing core seam is agreed.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrowed contract
recommendation.body: Sponsor the taxonomy after the trusted-emitter bypass is removed, schemaVersion is embedded in every event, and the dedicated plugin authorization API is reviewed with focused compatibility proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history ties the central diagnostic event architecture to this owner, making them the strongest routing candidate for the permanent core and Plugin SDK contract.
